Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up on latency & throughput requirements

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for a productive call earlier — good to learn more about FinPay's fraud-detection pipeline and where you're planning to use embeddings + runtime LLM prompts for triage. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can recommend the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private):

What I heard:
- Peak throughput target: ~500 requests/sec (batch size 1 for online scoring)
- P95 latency requirement: <= 150ms (max tolerated 200ms)
- Model candidate: open LLM (Llama 3 13B quantized) for lower TCO; considering experiments with a v2 model later
- Data controls: not fully regulated, but prefer VPC peering for traffic isolation later (not immediate blocker)

Open questions for you: could you confirm:
1) Is the 500 req/s estimate a sustained rate or spikes? If spikes, how long and how frequent?
2) Typical input sequence lengths (tokens) for the scoring path?
3) Any hard constraints on cold-start latency (first token) vs steady-state?

Next steps I propose:
- If the 500 req/s is sustained with tight p95 latency target, Dedicated capacity is usually a better fit — predictable throughput and reserved GPU pools let us hit low p95s without falling back.
- If traffic is bursty and you want to start quickly, Hosted API can be used with an autoscaling plan + canary to watch latency, but cost/latency may vary during spikes.

I attached a short performance worksheet (redwood-dedicated-performance-sheet.xlsx) with example configs and expected p95s for common models + our SLA summary. If you can reply with the three items above, I’ll loop in Rishi (SE) and Marissa (AM) to propose a short benchmark we can run against a representative payload.

Best,

Neha — thanks for the recap, that looks right. Quick answers below.

> 1) Is the 500 req/s estimate a sustained rate or spikes? If spikes, how long and how frequent?
It's a sustained peak for our busiest region during transaction hours (roughly 08:00–20:00 PT). We see a predictable plateau around 450–550 req/s for ~8–10 hours. There are rare higher spikes (~800 req/s) for 5–10 minutes when a partner batch finishes.

> 2) Typical input sequence lengths (tokens) for the scoring path?
Average ~120 tokens, 95th ~300 tokens (includes the prompt + metadata).

> 3) Any hard constraints on cold-start latency (first token) vs steady-state?
Cold-starts should be <500ms; steady-state p95 must be <=150ms. We can tolerate occasional brief degradation for the 5–10 minute partner spikes but need fallback to a cheaper model or queueing when that happens.

We’re leaning away from self-hosted on-prem at the moment due to ops overhead, but Dedicated capacity sounds promising. Please loop in your SE to sketch the bench plan.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Fraud Engineering, FinPay
